cultural.vision_reason: A traditional Ethiopian painting on parchment depicting Amhara/Ethiopian equestrian warriors and soldiers in ceremonial procession, with regalia (lion's mane cloak, silver ornaments, spears, swords) typical of Amhara nobility and warrior culture—clearly a work made in and depicting this tradition.

physical.title: painting
physical.summary: Painting on parchment depicting a group of Ethiopian equestrian warriors and foot soldiers in procession. The painting is on a yellow background. The group of equestrian warriors all ride horses with red leather saddle cloths, Ethiopian toe stirrups, and headgear, crupper and breaststraps with silver ornaments indicative of the riders' high status. The rider of the blue horse wears a lion's skin cloak (lemd) with lion's mane collar and a silver gilt armlet. He carries a long spear and a long curved sword in a red velvet sheath with a silver pommel. The rider to the left wears a skin lemd with cross decoration, an elaborate armlet and carries an Ethiopian curved sword (shotel). The foot soldiers all wear white shawls (shamma) with red borders. One of the foot soldiers on the far right carries a shield with silver ornaments and a pendant made of lion's mane. Four men on grey horses play double drums, one has a red embroidered umbrella with a silver finial in the form of a cross. Leading the procession is a man in a red cap with tassel and silver ornaments.
